WITH customer_spans AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           MIN(txn_date) AS first_day,
           MAX(txn_date) AS last_day,
           COUNT(DISTINCT txn_date) AS transaction_days
    FROM main.customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM main.customer_transactions) AS transactions,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT txn_type) FROM main.customer_transactions) AS transaction_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM main.customer_transactions
        WHERE customer_id IS NULL OR txn_type IS NULL OR txn_amount IS NULL
           OR date(txn_date) IS NULL OR txn_date <> date(txn_date)) AS incomplete_or_non_iso,
       (SELECT MIN(txn_amount) FROM main.customer_transactions) AS minimum_amount,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       MIN(first_day) AS first_day,
       MAX(first_day) AS latest_start,
       MIN(last_day) AS earliest_end,
       MAX(last_day) AS last_day,
       SUM(transaction_days) AS customer_transaction_days,
       SUM(CAST(julianday(last_day) - julianday(first_day) + 1 AS INTEGER)) AS days_within_customer_spans,
       SUM(CAST(julianday((SELECT MAX(last_day) FROM customer_spans)) - julianday(first_day) + 1 AS INTEGER)) AS days_through_latest_transaction
FROM customer_spans

item.text: The table contains 500 customers, and all first transacted in January 2020. I’ll carry each balance forward on days without transactions through April 28, the last date in the ledger. January balances will count toward February’s rolling averages.

arguments.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
daily_changes AS (
    SELECT customer_id, txn_date,
           SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_change
    FROM main.customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
customer_days(customer_id, balance_date, baseline_month) AS (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date), strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(txn_date))
    FROM daily_changes
    GROUP BY customer_id

    UNION ALL

    SELECT customer_id, date(balance_date, '+1 day'), baseline_month
    FROM customer_days
    WHERE balance_date < (SELECT MAX(txn_date) FROM daily_changes)
),
daily_balances AS (
    SELECT days.customer_id, days.balance_date, days.baseline_month,
           SUM(COALESCE(changes.net_change, 0)) OVER (
               PARTITION BY days.customer_id
               ORDER BY days.balance_date
               ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
           ) AS closing_balance
    FROM customer_days AS days
    LEFT JOIN daily_changes AS changes
        ON changes.customer_id = days.customer_id
       AND changes.txn_date = days.balance_date
),
rolling_averages AS (
    SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', balance_date) AS month, baseline_month,
           AVG(closing_balance) OVER trailing_30_days AS avg_balance,
           COUNT(*) OVER trailing_30_days AS days_in_window
    FROM daily_balances
    WINDOW trailing_30_days AS (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY balance_date
        ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    )
),
customer_monthly_maxima AS (
    SELECT customer_id, month,
           MAX(CASE WHEN avg_balance < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE avg_balance END) AS max_avg_balance
    FROM rolling_averages
    WHERE days_in_window = 30 AND month > baseline_month
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
)
SELECT month, SUM(max_avg_balance) AS total_max_30_day_avg_balance
FROM customer_monthly_maxima
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
